To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Ni-Al substrates have been developed with the graded structure, which are promising for the intermediate temperature solid oxide fuel cells (IT-SOFCs) and structured catalysts for the fuel reformers; (2) Ni-Al substrata with the graded structure have demonstrated high corrosion stability in the corrosive environment of the IT-SOFC; (3) Ni-Al substratum with the graded structure has been successfully tested as a support of the IT-SOF cell; (4)
new porous substrates with a graded structure for the solid oxide fuel cell and structured catalysts for the fuel reformer were developed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
development of novel composite foam substrates for intermediate-temperature SOFC and structured in-cell catalysts for fuels reforming.
the development of novel materials and technologies to support the next-generation of SOFCs.
development of the new composite foam substrata with the graded structure and composition for the intermediate temperature fuel cells and structured catalysts for in-cell reforming.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a new generation of SOFC with the graded structure and composition of the porous substrate is a promising approach to the high-performance and reliable power source.
the development of the new generation of the SOFCs with the graded structure of the anode substrate and in-cell reformer is possible and the concept can be realized.

the development of new composite substrates and structured catalysts for intermediate temperature solid oxide fuel cells is an effective and promising way for the commercialization of these fuel cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the developed composite substrates and catalysts are promising for the intermediate temperature solid oxide fuel cells operating on the fuels with a high carbon content.
the development of the structured catalytic materials and the substrate for intermediate-temperature SOFCs is an important and promising area of the research and development.

the developed Ni-Al foam substrates with high porosity and the graded pore structure are compatible with structured catalysts based on nanocomposite materials and can be used for fabrication of the intermediate temperature SOFCS with in-cell reforming.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structured catalysts with the graded structure and composition can be successfully used in the intermediate temperature solid oxide fuel cells operating on hydrocarbons.
the graded porous substrate is a key component of the SOFCs operating in the intermediate temperature mode and the structured catalysts for the in-cell reforming.

the graded structure of substrates and catalysts is the key factor in the design of the SOFCs with the internal reforming and that the graded structure can be obtained by the combination of different manufacturing methods.
